import java.util.*;
import java.io.*;

public class _1599_C {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        BufferedReader in = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
        PrintWriter out = new PrintWriter(System.out);
        StringTokenizer line = new StringTokenizer(in.readLine());
        int n = Integer.parseInt(line.nextToken());
        double p = Double.parseDouble(line.nextToken());
        int total = choose_three(n);
        for(int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            double prob = 0;
            // Case 1: Johnny studied i maps, opponent picks randomly
            // We need to calculate probability that the final map is one Johnny studied
            
            // Case 1: All 3 maps are from Johnny's studied maps (i maps)
            // Both players will discard maps from the 3 studied maps, system picks randomly from remaining
            // If both players only see studied maps, they might discard differently
            
            // Let's reconsider the problem:
            // System selects 3 maps from N total maps
            // Johnny studies i maps
            // Each player (Johnny and opponent) picks one of the 3 maps to discard
            // System then randomly selects one of the maps not picked by any player
            
            // For Johnny to play a studied map, we need to count scenarios where the final selected map is among the i studied ones
            
            // Case breakdown based on how many studied maps are in the initial 3:
            // Let k = number of studied maps in the 3 selected maps (k can be 0,1,2,3)
            
            // Probability of k studied maps in initial 3: C(i,k) * C(n-i, 3-k) / C(n,3)
            
            // Then, given k studied maps in the 3, we need to compute probability that final map is studied
            
            // If k=0: 0 studied maps, final map cannot be studied
            // If k=1: 1 studied, 2 unstudied
            //   Johnny wants to keep the studied one, opponent picks randomly
            //   Johnny discards one of the 3, opponent discards one of the 3
            //   If Johnny discards unstudied (2 choices), opponent might discard studied or unstudied
            //   If opponent discards same as Johnny, system picks from remaining 2
            //   If opponent discards different, system picks from remaining 1
            
            // Let's compute for k=1:
            // Maps: S, U1, U2 (S=studied, U=unstudied)
            // Johnny's strategy: discard unstudied (to keep S)
            // Opponent picks randomly among 3
            //   Opponent picks S (1/3): then Johnny discards U1, system picks from {U2, S} but S was picked by opponent? No - system picks from maps NOT picked by any player
            //   If Johnny discards U1, opponent discards S: remaining is U2, system picks U2 (unstudied)
            //   If Johnny discards U1, opponent discards U2: remaining is S, system picks S (studied)
            //   If Johnny discards U1, opponent discards U1: remaining are S, U2, system picks randomly (1/2 chance for S)
            
            // Actually, let's think more carefully:
            // Each player picks ONE map to discard. They pick simultaneously or Johnny knows opponent's choice? 
            // Problem says "each player must pick one of those three maps to be discarded" - typically this means they pick independently.
            // If both pick the same map to discard, then only one map is discarded, and system picks randomly from remaining 2.
            // If they pick different maps, then 2 maps are discarded, and system picks the remaining 1.
            
            // For k=1 (1 studied, 2 unstudied):
            // Johnny's optimal strategy: discard an unstudied map
            // Opponent picks randomly among 3 maps
            //   Opponent picks studied (prob 1/3): 
            //       Johnny discards unstudied (say U1), opponent discards S
            //       Discarded: U1 and S, remaining: U2 -> system picks U2 (unstudied)
            //   Opponent picks same unstudied as Johnny (prob 1/3 for each unstudied, so 2/3 total that opponent picks unstudied, but 1/3 chance it's the same one Johnny picked)
            //       Actually, if Johnny picks U1, opponent picks U1 with prob 1/3: discarded U1, remaining S, U2, system picks randomly (1/2 S)
            //       If opponent picks the other unstudied U2 (prob 1/3): discarded U1 and U2, remaining S, system picks S (studied)
            // So for k=1:
            //   prob(studied) = (1/3)*0 + (1/3)*(1/2) + (1/3)*1 = 0 + 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2
            
            // For k=2 (2 studied, 1 unstudied):
            // Maps: S1, S2, U
            // Johnny's strategy: discard U (to keep both studied)
            // Opponent picks randomly among 3
            //   Opponent picks U (1/3): discarded U twice, remaining S1,S2, system picks randomly (1 chance for studied)
            //   Opponent picks S1 (1/3): discarded U and S1, remaining S2, system picks S2 (studied)
            //   Opponent picks S2 (1/3): discarded U and S2, remaining S1, system picks S1 (studied)
            // So prob(studied) = 1
            
            // For k=3 (3 studied):
            // Maps: S1, S2, S3
            // Johnny's strategy: discard any (all are studied)
            // Opponent picks randomly among 3
            //   Opponent picks same as Johnny (1/3): discarded one map twice, remaining 2 studied, system picks randomly (1 chance for studied)
            //   Opponent picks different (2/3): discarded 2 maps, remaining 1 studied, system picks studied
            // So prob(studied) = 1
            
            // For k=0: prob(studied) = 0
            
            // Now compute overall probability:
            // P(k=0) = C(i,0)*C(n-i,3)/C(n,3) = C(n-i,3)/C(n,3)
            // P(k=1) = C(i,1)*C(n-i,2)/C(n,3)
            // P(k=2) = C(i,2)*C(n-i,1)/C(n,3)
            // P(k=3) = C(i,3)/C(n,3)
            
            // prob = P(k=1)*(1/2) + P(k=2)*1 + P(k=3)*1
            
            long c_n3 = choose_three(n);
            long c_i1_c_ni2 = (long)i * choose_two(n - i);
            long c_i2_c_ni1 = (long)choose_two(i) * (n - i);
            long c_i3 = choose_three(i);
            
            prob = (double)(c_i1_c_ni2 * 1/2 + c_i2_c_ni1 + c_i3) / c_n3;
            
            if(prob >= p) {
                out.println(i);
                break;
            }
        }
        in.close();
        out.close();
    }
    static long choose_two(int n) {
        if(n < 2) return 0;
        return (long)n * (n - 1) / 2;
    }
    static long choose_three(int n) {
        if(n < 3) return 0;
        return (long)n * (n - 1) * (n - 2) / 6;
    }
}
